rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here يسري means that the night moves on, passes, and comes to its end.
rows.anchor: إذا يسر } إذا يمضي كما قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another lexical explanation takes the night’s going as traveling through it.
rows.anchor: أو يقال : سراها هو السير فيها

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada interprets يسري as the night arriving and drawing near.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة : { إذا يسر } أي إذا جاء وأقبل

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most exegetes understand the oath as referring to night generally, not one particular night, comparing other general descriptions of night.
rows.anchor: أكثر المفسرين على أنه ليس المراد منه ليلة مخصوصة بل العموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternation of night and day and their changing lengths are a great blessing and signs of a wise, all-knowing director, making night worthy of an oath.
rows.anchor: ولأن نعمة الله بتعاقب الليل والنهار واختلاف مقاديرهما على الخلق عظيمة

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Mقاتل identifies the night as the night of Muzdalifa and reads يسري as travel taking place within it, like a night named for sleeping or staying awake in it.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل : هي ليلة المزدلفة فقوله : { إذا يسر } أي إذا يسار فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The journey through that night begins with departure from Arafat for Muzdalifa.
rows.anchor: وهي ليلة يقع السري في أولها عند الدفع من عرفات إلى المزدلفة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet brought forward his vulnerable family members during this night.
rows.anchor: كما روي أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام كان يقدم ضعفة أهله في هذه الليل

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi‘i allows this early departure only after the middle of the night.
rows.anchor: وإنما يجوز ذلك عند الشافعي رحمه الله بعد نصف الليل

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj reports a reading that retains the final yāʾ in يسري, but prefers its deletion because verse endings commonly drop yāʾs and the kasra signals it.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : قرئ { إذا يسر } بإثبات الياء ، ثم قال : وحذفها أحب إلي

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ says Arabs may delete yāʾ and rely on the preceding kasra; he adduces poetic usage as evidence.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء : والعرب قد تحذف الياء وتكتفي بكسرة ما قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited poem’s form تعط exemplifies yāʾ deletion, which is especially apt at a verse ending.
rows.anchor: كفاك كف ما يبقى درهما *** جودا وأخرى تعط بالسيف الدما

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali explains that pauses and rhyme endings permit change: even sound consonants change at pauses, so letters resembling additions may also be deleted.
rows.anchor: أجاب أبو علي فقال : القول في ذلك أن الفواصل والقوافي موضع وقف

rows.speaker: من أثبت الياء
rows.claim: Those retaining yāʾ in both connected and paused speech argue that verbs keep it at pause, unlike nouns such as قاض and غاز.
rows.anchor: وأما من أثبت الياء في يسري في الوصل والوقف فإنه يقول : الفعل لا يحذف منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حجر means intellect, named because it restrains a person from what is improper; عقل, نهية, and حصاة likewise suggest restraint or keeping count.
rows.anchor: الحجر العقل سمي به لأنه يمنع عن الوقوع فيما لا ينبغي

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ says a person ذو حجر is self-commanding and controlled; intellect is named حجر because it restrains wrongdoing, from the verb for restricting someone.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء : والعرب تقول إنه لذو حجر إذا كان قاهرا لنفسه ضابطا لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question whether there is an oath is rhetorical confirmation, like asking whether a striking proof is evidence.
rows.anchor: استفهام والمراد منه التأكيد كمن ذكر حجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A discerning person sees extraordinary signs of divine oneness and lordship in the sworn things; their signs point to their Creator.
rows.anchor: أن ما أقسم الله تعالى به من هذه الأشياء فيه عجائب ودلائل على التوحيد والربوبية

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qadi argues that the verse’s emphatic oath is by the Lord of these created things, since emphatic oaths are made by God and people are forbidden to swear by them.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي : وهذه الآية تدل على ما قلنا : أن القسم واقع برب هذه الأمور

rows.speaker: جماعة من المفسرين
rows.claim: A group says Hell will be brought at Resurrection bound with seventy thousand reins, each pulled by seventy thousand angels; it will strain as if to escape and would burn the gathering if released.
rows.anchor: قال جماعة من المفسرين : جيء بها يوم القيامة مزمومة بسبعين ألف زمام

rows.speaker: الأصوليون
rows.claim: The theologians say Hell does not leave its place; being brought forth means being exposed so creation sees it and the unbeliever recognizes his destination.
rows.anchor: قال الأصوليون : ومعلوم أنها لا تنفك عن مكانها ، فالمراد { وبرزت } أي ظهرت حتى رآها الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The syntax supplies a temporal condition: when the earth is crushed and the other events occur, then that day the human remembers.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن تقدير الكلام : إذا دكت الأرض ، وحصل كذا وكذا فيومئذ يتذكر الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that a person recalls having wrongly devoted worldly effort to this life instead of making the afterlife the goal.
rows.anchor: أنه يتذكر ما فرط فيه لأنه حين كان في الدنيا كانت همته تحصيل الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation makes يتذكر mean taking heed: those who ignored admonition in worldly life become admonished in the next and wish to return.
rows.anchor: يتذكر أي يتعظ ، والمعنى أنه ما كان يتعظ في الدنيا فيصير في الآخرة متعظا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan is reported to interpret the remembering as repentance.
rows.anchor: يتذكر يتوب وهو مروي عن الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent contradiction between remembering and the question how remembrance could help is resolved by supplying “benefit”: how could he benefit from remembrance then?
rows.anchor: واعلم أن بين قوله : { يتذكر } وبين قوله : { وأنى له الذكرى } تناقضا فلابد من إضمار المضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author holds that accepting repentance is not rationally obligatory for God; the verse says the sinner’s eventual repentance will not benefit him.
rows.anchor: قبول التوبة عندنا غير واجب على الله عقلا

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazilites maintain that accepting repentance is rationally obligatory.
rows.anchor: وقالت المعتزلة : هو واجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His argument is that people recognize their worldly choices were wrong and regret them, thereby repenting, yet the verse denies that this repentance benefits them.
rows.anchor: الإنسان يعلم في الآخرة أن الذي يعمله في الدنيا لم يكن أصلح له وإن الذي تركه كان أصلح له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says their regret was only fear of punishment, not regret for wrongdoing, so it was not valid repentance; the author replies that useful regret must be for the wrongness itself, making it valid repentance despite nonacceptance.
rows.anchor: فإن قيل القوم : إنما ندموا على أفعالهم لا لوجه قبحها بل لترتب العقاب عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading has the speaker wish that, during worldly life, he had prepared deeds for the everlasting afterlife; it is called “my life” because true life is there.
rows.anchor: في الدنيا التي كانت حياتي فيها منقطعة ، لحياتي هذه التي هي دائمة غير منقطعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reading says Hell’s people are effectively lifeless despite not dying; the speaker wishes he had done deeds that would save him from Hell and make him among the living.
rows.anchor: فياليتني قدمت عملا يوجب نجاتي من النار حتى أكون من الأحياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third reading takes the phrase as wishing he had acted during his lifetime in the world.
rows.anchor: وثالثها : أن يكون المعنى : فياليتني قدمت وقت حياتي في الدنيا

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazilites infer that people had genuine choice and will and were not prevented from obedience or driven into sin.
rows.anchor: استدلت المعتزلة بهذه الآية على أن الاختيار كان في أيديهم ومعلقا بقصدهم وإرادتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author replies that if a person’s intention depends on another intention, the chain regresses infinitely; if it depends on God’s intention, Muʿtazilism is refuted.
rows.anchor: فقصدهم إن كان معلقا بقصد آخر لزم التسلسل ، وإن كان معلقا بقصد الله فقد بطل الاعتزال

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: The author of al-Kashshaf derives كبَد from liver pain and swelling, extended to every hardship; مكابدة comes from this root.
rows.anchor: إن الكبد أصله من قولك كبد الرجل كبدا فهو كبد إذا وجعت كبده

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Others derive كبَد from severity and thickness, as milk thickens and the liver is thickened blood; on this account the hardship sense precedes the organ name.
rows.anchor: الكبد شدة الأمر ومنه تكبد اللبن إذا غلظ واشتد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two etymologies differ over direction: one derives hardship from the organ, the other derives the organ’s name from the sense of hardship and thickness.
rows.anchor: والفرق بين القولين أن الأول جعل اسم الكبد موضوعا للكبد ، ثم اشتقت منه الشدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second lexical view understands كبَد as uprightness and straightness.
rows.anchor: أن الكبد هو الاستواء والاستقامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third lexical view understands it as severity of constitution and physical strength.
rows.anchor: أن الكبد شدة الخلق والقوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If كبَد means hardship, it may cover worldly hardships: human life passes through pregnancy, nursing, earning a livelihood, and death.
rows.anchor: أي خلقناه أطوارا كلها شدة ومشقة ، تارة في بطن الأم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan applies the hardship to religion: people struggle to give thanks in ease, endure adversity patiently, and bear the trials of worship.
rows.anchor: يكابد الشكر على السراء ، والصبر على الضراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife reading includes death, questioning by the angel, the grave’s darkness, resurrection, judgment before God, and arrival in Paradise or Hell.
rows.anchor: فالموت ومساءلة الملك وظلمة القبر ، ثم البعث والعرض على الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the comprehensive reading that كبَد includes all forms of hardship.
rows.anchor: وأما الرابع : وهو يكون اللفظ محمولا على الكل فهو الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He adds that worldly pleasure is only relief from pain: eating relieves hunger and clothing relieves heat or cold, so a person has pain or temporary escape into another pain.
rows.anchor: ليس في هذه الدنيا لذة البتة ، بل ذاك يظن أنه لذة فهو خلاص عن الألم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This hardship argument entails resurrection: a merciful, wise Creator would not make pain the final purpose; mere nonexistence would suffice if neither pain nor pleasure were intended, while worldly pleasure is absent.
rows.anchor: فإذا لابد بعد هذه الدار من دار أخرى ، لتكون تلك الدار دار السعادات واللذات والكرمات

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: On the uprightness reading, Ibn Abbas says humans stand erect while other animals walk bent; this form is a favor.
rows.anchor: أي قائما منتصبا ، والحيوانات الأخر تمشي منكسة

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: On the strength reading, al-Kalbi says the verse was revealed about Abu al-Ashadd of Banu Jumah, who was so strong that leather pulled from under his feet tore while his feet remained steady.
rows.anchor: نزلت هذه الآية في رجل من بني جمح يكنى أبا الأشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the first interpretation, hardship, best fits the verse.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن اللائق بالآية هو الوجه الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prepositions في and لام are close in meaning, but في also portrays hardship as a surrounding container, enclosing the person in toil and trial.
rows.anchor: إنما أنت في العناء والنصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some restrict الإنسان to the particular strong man just described; most take it generally, while allowing that his action occasioned the revelation.
rows.anchor: منهم من قال : المراد بالإنسان إنسان معين

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Layth glosses تلا يتلو as following something.
rows.anchor: تلا يتلو إذا تبع شيئا

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: One view says the moon follows the sun’s light by remaining visible after sunset during the first half of the month.
rows.anchor: وهو قول عطاء عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: قتادة والكلبي
rows.claim: Qatada and al-Kalbi say the moon follows the sun in setting on the night of the new crescent.
rows.anchor: وهو قول قتادة والكلبي

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ takes following to mean receiving light from the sun, as one person follows another by taking from him.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء : المراد من هذا التلو هو أن القمر يأخذ الضوء من الشمس

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the moon follows the sun when it becomes rounded and full, matching the sun in brightness during the white nights.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : تلاها حين استدار وكمل ، فكأنه يتلو الشمس في الضياء والنور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view sees the moon as following in apparent size and in how its motion affects worldly interests; astronomy shows a special relation between moon and sun.
rows.anchor: أنه يتلوها في كبر الجرم بحسب الحس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day appears as the darkness of night departs.
rows.anchor: أي ظهر بزوال ظلمة الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the day appears and is unveiled with sunrise.
rows.anchor: أو ظهر وانكشف بطلوع الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse answers the preceding oath: people’s deeds differ, and their recompenses differ accordingly.
rows.anchor: هذا الجواب القسم ، فأقسم تعالى بهذه الأشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: شتى is the broken plural of شتيت and conveys separation: deeds are far apart because some are guidance and others error, leading respectively to Gardens or Fire.
rows.anchor: وشتى جمع شتيت مثل مرضى ومريض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He links the contrast to verses saying Paradise’s people differ from Hell’s people and believers differ from the wicked.
rows.anchor: لا يستوي أصحاب النار وأصحاب الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also cites the claim that sinners and believers cannot be treated as equal in life or death.
rows.anchor: أم حسب الذين اجترحوا السيئات أن نجعلهم كالذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further comparison contrasts shade with scorching heat.
rows.anchor: ولا الظل ولا الحرور

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The exegetes say this verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr and Abu Sufyan.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون : نزلت هذه الآية في أبي بكر وأبي سفيان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the return to the lowest state as reaching decrepit old age, as in the verse about being returned to the most feeble age.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : يريد أرذل العمر

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba says the lowest are the weak, infirm, helpless people; old age weakens hearing, sight, reason, and ability, leaving one unable to do good.
rows.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة : السافلون هم الضعفاء والزمنى ، ومن لا يستطيع حيلة ولا يجد سبيلا

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ says singular أسفل سافل would be grammatically possible, but the plural is used because الإنسان is singular in wording and plural in meaning.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء : ولو كانت أسفل سافل لكان صوابا ، لأن لفظ الإنسان واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural-by-meaning construction is paralleled by a verse that shifts from singular wording about one who brings truth to plural “those” who are mindful.
rows.anchor: والذي جاء بالصدق وصدق به أولئك هم المتقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also cites a verse that begins with singular الإنسان and shifts to plural pronouns.
rows.anchor: وإنا إذا أذقنا الإنسان منا رحمة فرح بها وإن تصبهم

rows.speaker: مجاهد والحسن
rows.claim: Mujahid and al-Hasan interpret the lowest state as being returned to the Fire.
rows.anchor: والقول الثاني : ما ذكره مجاهد والحسن ثم رددناه إلى النار

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali says Hell’s gates are arranged one below another and the lowest level is filled first, explaining the phrase as the lowest of the low.
rows.anchor: قال علي عليه السلام : وضع أبواب جهنم بعضها أسفل من بعض فيبدأ بالأسفل فيملأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in الإنسان may refer to humanity as a class or to a previously known individual.
rows.anchor: الألف واللام في الإنسان ، يحتمل أن تكون للجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the generic reading, the verse means humanity generally is in loss, as the following exception for believers indicates.
rows.anchor: أن المراد منه الجنس وهو كقولهم : كثر الدرهم في أيدي الناس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies a specific group of polytheists: al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, al-As ibn Waʾil, and al-Aswad ibn Abd al-Muttalib.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : يريد جماعة من المشركين كالوليد بن المغيرة

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says the verse was revealed about Abu Lahab.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل : نزلت في أبي لهب

rows.speaker: خبر مرفوع
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet identifies the person as Abu Jahl; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: وفي خبر مرفوع إنه أبو جهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says these people used to claim Muhammad was in loss, so God swore that the opposite was true.
rows.anchor: وروي أن هؤلاء كانوا يقولون : إن محمدا لفي خسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خسر means loss or decrease, like خسران and كفران, and can mean losing one’s capital.
rows.anchor: معناه النقصان وذهاب رأس المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If الإنسان is generic, loss means wasting one’s self and lifetime, except for believers who gain everlasting bliss through them.
rows.anchor: إذا حملنا الإنسان على الجنس كان معنى الخسر هلاك نفسه وعمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If الإنسان means unbelievers, loss is error and disbelief, from which those who believe escape into profit.
rows.anchor: وإن حملنا لفظ الإنسان على الكافر كان المراد كونه في الضلالة والكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite خسر may magnify the loss: it is immense beyond human comprehension because sin is against God and against great blessings.
rows.anchor: فإن حملنا على الأول كان المعنى إن الإنسان لفي خسر عظيم لا يعلم كنهه إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the indefinite may belittle the loss by implying human loss is less than Satan’s, a consoling reminder that someone is more disobedient.
rows.anchor: وإن حملناه على الثاني كان المعنى أن خسران الإنسان دون خسران الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the magnifying interpretation is the correct one.
rows.anchor: والتأويل الصحيح هو الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although الإنسان is involved in many losses, the singular wording points to the true loss: deprivation of serving God; loss of Paradise and punishment are negligible by comparison.
rows.anchor: أن الخسر الحقيقي هو حرمانه عن خدمة ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose of creation is worship, so all other purposes are negligible by comparison.
rows.anchor: ثم قال : { وما خلقت الجن والإنس إلا ليعبدون } أي لما كان هذا المقصود أجل المقاصد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic إن and lām, together with في, portray a person immersed and surrounded by loss.
rows.anchor: قوله : { لفي خسر } يفيد أنه كالمغمور في الخسران ، وأنه أحاط به من كل جانب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle إن adds emphasis to the assertion of loss.
rows.anchor: كلمة إن ، ، فإنها للتأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One construal takes في خسر as being on the path to loss, as with consuming an orphan’s wealth “in their bellies” when the outcome is Fire.
rows.anchor: في قوله تعالى : { لفي خسر } أي في طريق الخسر ، وهذا كقوله في أكل أموال اليتامى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another construal says no person escapes loss because life is capital that is continually spent.
rows.anchor: أن الإنسان لا ينفك عن خسر ، لأن الخسر هو تضييع رأس المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every hour spent in sin is loss; even permissible activity loses time without lasting effect, although it could have been used for enduring work.
rows.anchor: فإن كانت مصروفة إلى المعصية فلا شك في الخسران ، وإن كانت مشغولة بالمباحات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even worship can fall short: devotion has endlessly higher degrees as knowledge of God’s majesty grows, so settling for a lower degree is a kind of loss.
rows.anchor: مراتب الخضوع والخشوع لله غير متناهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity tends toward loss because afterlife-directed motives are hidden while worldly motives—senses, desire, and anger—are obvious, leaving most people absorbed in the world.
rows.anchor: وتقريره أن سعادة الإنسان في حب الآخرة والإعراض عن الدنيا ، ثم إن الأسباب الداعية إلى الآخرة خفية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent contrast with Surah al-Tin is resolved by distinguishing bodily conditions there from the soul’s conditions here.
rows.anchor: قلنا : المذكور في سورة التين أحوال البدن ، وههنا أحوال النفس فلا تناقض بين القولين
